misread_or_logic.why: The code contradicts the visible example or uses a wrong algorithm; a short rule cannot supply the algorithm, but running the example exposes the contradiction.

knowledge_gap.fixable_by_prompt_rule: yes, if the bank holds the definition
knowledge_gap.why: The student does not know a named sequence or formula; feedback cannot conjure it, a retrieved definition can.

careless_code_error.why: Undefined names, bad calls and syntax slips produce a precise error message when the example is run.

name_mismatch.why: The function is named differently from the example call; an alias repairs it without any model call.

hidden_wrong_output_spec.why: The statement is ambiguous and the hidden tests encode one convention (re.search, None on no match, split(' ')).

hidden_crash_edge.why: Crash on empty or negative input that the visible example does not exercise.

reference_quirk.why: The reference solution behaves unexpectedly; no sensible rule predicts it.

missing_base_or_empty_case.why: Recursion without a base case or max() of an empty container.

hardcoded_from_example.why: A size or exponent was copied from the single example instead of computed.

hidden_wrong_output_edge.why: Bit trick breaks for negative operands.

efficiency.why: Linear divisor loop times out for n near 10**9.

rules.text: Polygonal numbers, n-th term: triangular n*(n+1)//2, pentagonal n*(3*n-1)//2, hexagonal n*(2*n-1), heptagonal n*(5*n-3)//2, octagonal n*(3*n-2), nonagonal n*(7*n-5)//2, decagonal n*(4*n-3).
Centered k-gonal number, n-th term: k*n*(n-1)//2 + 1. Centered square 2*n*(n-1)+1, centered pentagonal 5*n*(n-1)//2+1, centered hexagonal 3*n*(n-1)+1, star number 6*n*(n-1)+1.
Solid figurate numbers, n-th term: tetrahedral n*(n+1)*(n+2)//6, square pyramidal n*(n+1)*(2*n+1)//6, octahedral n*(2*n*n+1)//3.

Woodall numbers are n*2**n - 1 (1, 7, 23, 63, 159, 383, ...); Cullen n*2**n + 1; Mersenne 2**n - 1; Carol (2**n - 1)**2 - 2; Kynea (2**n + 1)**2 - 2. To test membership, generate terms in a loop until they reach the input.

Recurrences: Lucas L0=2, L1=1, L(n)=L(n-1)+L(n-2). Pell P0=0, P1=1, P(n)=2*P(n-1)+P(n-2). Jacobsthal J0=0, J1=1, J(n)=J(n-1)+2*J(n-2); Jacobsthal-Lucas starts 2, 1 with the same step. Perrin 3, 0, 2 then P(n)=P(n-2)+P(n-3); Padovan 1, 1, 1 with the same step.
Newman-Conway sequence: P(1)=P(2)=1 and P(n)=P(P(n-1))+P(n-P(n-1)). Fill a list bottom-up from index 1.
Newman-Shanks-Williams numbers: S(0)=1, S(1)=1, S(n)=2*S(n-1)+S(n-2), giving 1, 1, 3, 7, 17, 41, ...

Catalan C(n)=math.comb(2*n, n)//(n+1). Bell numbers: build the Bell triangle, each row starting with the last value of the previous row. Stirling (second kind) S(n,k)=k*S(n-1,k)+S(n-1,k-1). Eulerian A(n,m)=(n-m)*A(n-1,m-1)+(m+1)*A(n-1,m) with A(n,0)=1 and A(n,m)=0 for m>=n. Delannoy D(m,n)=D(m-1,n)+D(m-1,n-1)+D(m,n-1).
Binomial sums: all C(n,k) add to 2**n; even-index terms add to 2**(n-1), odd-index terms too; sum of C(n,k)**2 is C(2n,n); sum of C(n,k)*C(n,k+1) is C(2n,n-1). Use math.comb.

Armstrong number: sum(d**k for each digit d) == n where k is the number of digits (not always 3). Proper divisors exclude the number itself. Perfect: sum of proper divisors == n. Amicable pair: a != b, sumdiv(a) == b and sumdiv(b) == a. Harshad: n % digit_sum == 0.

Solids (use math.pi): cylinder lateral 2*pi*r*h, total 2*pi*r*(r+h), volume pi*r*r*h. Cone slant l=sqrt(r*r+h*h), lateral pi*r*l, total pi*r*(r+l), volume pi*r*r*h/3. Sphere area 4*pi*r*r, volume 4/3*pi*r**3. Cube 6*a*a, lateral 4*a*a. Cuboid 2*(l*w+l*h+w*h), lateral 2*h*(l+w). Square pyramid b*b+2*b*slant. Tetrahedron area sqrt(3)*a*a.

Plane figures: trapezium area (a+b)/2*h and median (a+b)/2; rhombus p*q/2; sector pi*r*r*angle/360; arc length 2*pi*r*angle/360; regular polygon with n sides of length s: n*s*s/(4*tan(pi/n)); triangle 0.5*b*h; ellipse pi*a*b.
Wind chill index (v in km/h, t in Celsius): 13.12 + 0.6215*t - 11.37*v**0.16 + 0.3965*t*v**0.16, then round as the task says.
Months with 31 days: 1, 3, 5, 7, 8, 10, 12. Months with 30 days: 4, 6, 9, 11. February (2) has 28 or 29 days and belongs to neither group.

Bit idioms: exactly one bit set (power of two, or two numbers differ in one bit via x = a ^ b) is `x > 0 and x & (x - 1) == 0`; lowest set bit `x & -x`; set bit i `x | (1 << i)`; clear `x & ~(1 << i)`; toggle `x ^ (1 << i)`; highest bit position `x.bit_length() - 1`; `bin(x).count('1')` only for x >= 0.
Define the function with exactly the name used in the example assert, copied character for character, even if it looks misspelled or is a built-in name.
Handle empty input first, e.g. `if not items: return []` (or `0`, `''` as fits). Never index `[0]`, take `% len(x)`, or call `max()`/`min()` without `default=` on something that may be empty.
Inputs may be negative or zero: use `abs(n)` before a `str(n)` digit loop and before `bin(n)` tricks.
For text-pattern tasks use `re.search`, which finds the pattern anywhere in the string, not `re.match`, unless the task says the string must start with the pattern.
When nothing is found, return `None` itself, not a tuple or list filled with None; return a finished value, never a generator (`yield`).
The input mixes strings and numbers: keep only the numbers first, `nums = [x for x in items if isinstance(x, int)]`, then compute on `nums`.
Give every recursion a base case that stops at 0 (`if n <= 0: return 0` or the right start value) and cache it with `@functools.lru_cache(None)`; prefer a loop that fills a list for sequences.
Split on the exact character the task names, e.g. `s.split(' ')`; bare `split()` merges whitespace and drops empty strings.
Loop divisors only up to `int(n ** 0.5)`: when `i` divides `n` count both `i` and `n // i` (once if equal). Inputs can be near 10**9, so an O(n) loop is too slow.
Return the same type and shape as the expected value in the example: a tuple stays a tuple, nested lists stay nested, a converted string is returned as a string (not True/False).
Never hard-code a size, exponent or count taken from the example (such as 4 rows or power 3); compute it from the input with `len(...)`.
Begin the code with a comment `# example:` stating in one line how the example input becomes the example output; the function must return exactly that value for that input.

codemods.what: If the function called in the example is not defined, bind that name to the single (or closest-named) function the answer defines.

codemods.name: add_missing_imports
codemods.what: Prepend imports for standard-library modules and well-known helpers that are used but never imported.
